nodes.name: On Telegram Event
nodes.notes: Native push trigger — telegram calls this workflow the moment the event happens (no polling). Credential: Telegram bot token. Same bot token as the Telegram node (@BotFather → /newbot).

nodes.name: Pull Fresh Items (API)
nodes.notes: GET https://api.example.com/v1/requests — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Newest First
nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

nodes.name: Trim to Digest Size
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 15 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Summarize Content (AI)
nodes.notes: Map-reduce summarization chain — handles long content without blowing the context window. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: Anthropic Chat Model
nodes.notes: Chat model powering the AI step (model: claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929). Swap providers here without rewiring. Credential: Anthropic API key. console.anthropic.com → Settings → API Keys.

nodes.name: Post Digest to Telegram
nodes.notes: Sends a Telegram message to the configured chat — the same bot can also receive replies, so this doubles as a two-way ops channel. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Telegram bot token. Message @BotFather on Telegram → /newbot → copy the token.

nodes.name: Post Digest to Slack
nodes.notes: Posts a message to Slack (#ai-ops) — a low-latency way for the team to see automation activity without checking a dashboard. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Slack OAuth2. Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.

nodes.name: Confirm All Sends
nodes.notes: Rejoins 2 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Archive Digest in Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Request Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per request (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.notes: GET https://enrichment.example.com/v2/lookup — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.name: Fold In Enrichment Fields
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes enrichedAt, enrichmentSource. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Serialize Run Output (CSV)
nodes.notes: Serializes items to a CSV binary file.

nodes.notes: Creates a new page in the Notion database — the title is pulled straight from the item's key field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. # Summarize meeting notes with Telegram

**Pattern:** AI Summarize & Route · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers task-automation work end to end across Telegram, Google Sheets, Slack and Notion.

It moves through 19 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. On Telegram Event
2. Pull Fresh Items (API)
3. Newest First
4. Trim to Digest Size
5. Summarize Content (AI)
6. Anthropic Chat Model
7. Post Digest to Telegram
8. Post Digest to Slack
9. Confirm All Sends
10. Archive Digest in Google Sheets
11. Fingerprint for Idempotency
12. Drop Already-Processed Items
13. Enrich with Reference Data
14. Fold In Enrichment Fields
15. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
16. Archive Row Snapshot
17. Summarize Run Stats
18. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
19. Send Summary to Telegram

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Telegram → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing task-automation work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

On Telegram Event → Pull Fresh Items (API) → Newest First → Trim to Digest Size → Summarize Content (AI) → Anthropic Chat Model → Post Digest to Telegram → Post Digest to Slack → Confirm All Sends → Archive Digest in Google Sheets → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Telegram → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Telegram → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Telegram and Google Sheets aligned by hand for task automation
- Pushing task-automation events into Telegram and Google Sheets the moment they land, not on the next poll
- Task automation work where "Pull Fresh Items (API)" is still a manual step before Telegram
- Task automation work that only reaches Telegram when a webhook arrives, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Telegram and Google Sheets in step for task automation, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Telegram or Google Sheets are skipped, across all 22 nodes of this task-automation build
- A failed Telegram or Google Sheets call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 22 nodes in this task-automation build
- The task-automation AI step is isolated from Telegram, so models swap without touching the other 22 nodes
- Fans the same result out to Slack in the same run, for task automation

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Anthropic API key; Google OAuth2 / service account; Notion integration token; Slack OAuth2; Telegram bot token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Summarization uses a Chain, not an Agent, because the step is fixed — there's no decision about which tool to call, just 'summarize this text.' Posting to multiple channels runs as parallel branches, not sequential sends, so a slow API on one channel never delays the message that was already ready on another.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Add a third notification channel and watch the Merge node's input count update.
2. Change 'Trim to Digest Size' from 15 to 5 and see how it narrows the summary's scope.
3. Swap the Summarization Chain for a Q&A Chain to answer questions instead of just recapping.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Telegram bot token**
Same bot token as the Telegram node (@BotFather → /newbot).
_Gotcha:_ A bot supports only one webhook at a time — a second workflow listening on the same bot steals the updates.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Anthropic API key**
console.anthropic.com → Settings → API Keys.
_Gotcha:_ Requires purchased credit.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your task automation process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Telegram: the bot token is a bearer credential — rotate it if it ever appears in an execution log.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole task-automation payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.
